# `js/regexp-prefer-lookaround`

**A captured text put back unchanged is matched with a lookaround**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-js` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-js` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | no preset — name it in `[rules]` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | none — severity only |
| **Fix** | `suggest` — `codelaw fix --unsafe` applies it; review the diff, it can change behaviour (matching with a lookaround changes which text a global replacement consumes, so overlapping matches can differ) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.0 |
| **Ported from** | `eslint-plugin-regexp/prefer-lookaround` |

## What it checks

A replacement that starts or ends with `$1`, where group 1 is the pattern's first or last element, uses a lookbehind or lookahead instead: `s.replace(/(a)b/, '$1c')` is `s.replace(/(?<=a)b/, 'c')`.

**Why:** The capture and the reinsertion say less than a lookaround.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-js
pip install codelaw-rules-js
```

**No preset turns it on.** Load its pack through any preset (`codelaw:js/recommended` here), then name the rule in `[rules]`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:js/recommended"]

[rules]
"js/regexp-prefer-lookaround" = "error"
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"js/regexp-prefer-lookaround" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/regexp-prefer-lookaround" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"js/regexp-prefer-lookaround" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"js/regexp-prefer-lookaround" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"js/regexp-prefer-lookaround" = { severity = "warn" }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "js/regexp-prefer-lookaround": {"severity": "warn"}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore js/regexp-prefer-lookaround: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore js/regexp-prefer-lookaround expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule js/regexp-prefer-lookaround --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain js/regexp-prefer-lookaround       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule js/regexp-prefer-lookaround  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>               # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Turn the group into a lookbehind (or lookahead) and drop the `$1`.

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

```js
s.replace(/(a)b/g, '$1c');
```

#### Do

```js
s.replace(/(?<=a)b/g, 'c');
```

### JSX

#### Don't

```jsx
s.replace(/(a)b/g, '$1c');
```

#### Do

```jsx
s.replace(/(?<=a)b/g, 'c');
```

### TypeScript

#### Don't

```ts
s.replace(/(a)b/g, '$1c');
```

#### Do

```ts
s.replace(/(?<=a)b/g, 'c');
```

### TSX

#### Don't

```tsx
s.replace(/(a)b/g, '$1c');
```

#### Do

```tsx
s.replace(/(?<=a)b/g, 'c');
```
